item.title: 'From the river to the sea': Hundreds rally across Israel advocating Jewish-Arab gov
item.description: Around 300 demonstrators gathered in Jerusalem, Tel Aviv, and Haifa to demand a Jewish-Arab government. Protesters held signs advocating for freedom and inclusive governance, reflecting their unified call. The demonstrations coincided with ongoing vote counting following Israel's closely contested election. Pro-Netanyahu parties secured 53 seats, while the opposing bloc held 48, leaving no clear majority. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot emphasized a need for change, criticizing Netanyahu's government.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Sunshine Buns, started in 2022 by four Utah friends, raised $7 million
item.description: Sunshine Buns has successfully secured $7 million in Series A funding, allowing them to broaden their store presence. Founded by four friends using a family cinnamon roll recipe, their frozen delights are now featured in major retailers like Target and Costco. This new funding will support production and marketing efforts, and the founders attribute their success to local mentors and the nurturing startup community in Utah.

item.title: Diver searching the bottom of England’s River Wear has pulled a huge three legged iron cauldron
item.description: An ancient iron cauldron, potentially from the medieval or Iron Age, was found submerged under water. Underwater archaeologist Gary Bankhead led a team of divers in this ambitious recovery mission. Experts are currently investigating the cauldron's design and historical relevance. This intriguing find prompts speculation about its origin and journey into the river, with plans underway for a public exhibition at a nearby museum.

item.title: Florida man pays HOA debt five days after home auction; court overturns sale cancellation
item.description: A Florida homeowner paid his outstanding homeowners' association fees five days after his property was sold at a foreclosure auction in October 2024. The sale was subsequently cancelled, but the winning bidder challenged the decision, saying it had not been heard. Nearly two years later, a Florida appeals court overturned the cancellation and ordered a fresh hearing.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Historian Charles Greig donated 50 paintings and watercolours to Tate; from colonial India
item.description: In a remarkable gesture, Tate London has received a donation of 50 artworks from the British colonial era in India, showcasing the talents of both Indian and European artists. This diverse collection, meticulously curated by British art historian Charles Greig over 40 years, will be publicly exhibited at Tate Britain in 2028, enhancing public access to these invaluable historical pieces and underscoring the importance of art preservation.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Texas barber returns $128,514 found at ATM despite rent struggles
item.description: In Lewisville, Texas, a barber stumbled upon two bags at an ATM, one filled with an astonishing $128,514 in cash. Struggling with rent and financial issues, he made the commendable choice to report this to the authorities. The bags belonged to a Brink’s team who had accidentally left them behind. Though no financial reward was given, the barber's honesty was recognized and celebrated by the police.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Georgia siblings fight over 95-year-old mother's care and assets; court backs daughter
item.description: A dispute between three siblings over their 95-year-old mother's care reached the Georgia Court of Appeals after one son restricted his sister's visits and questions emerged over the handling of their mother's money. The woman, who has advanced dementia, had previously authorised her son to manage her affairs. However, the court upheld her daughter's appointment as guardian.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: The UK plans to send giant robotic claws into orbit to grab two dead satellites; 2029 mission
item.description: In a groundbreaking initiative, the UK plans to unveil a pioneering spacecraft in 2029, designed specifically for the cleanup of space debris. Utilizing advanced robotic arms, the mission aims to snatch up and incinerate inactive satellites, tackling the escalating issue of orbital pollution that threatens current satellite operations. A nationwide competition to name the spacecraft is in progress, underscoring the project's significance in fostering sustainable space practices.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Maui Estate Fetches $18.5 Million: Renovated Makena home tops 2026 sale; big price cut reflects cooling market
item.description: Recently, a stunning oceanfront estate in Makena, Maui, fetched a remarkable $18.5 million. After undergoing extensive renovations to boost its allure, this property saw an adjustment in its listing price from an initially higher value. While Hawaii's ultra-luxury housing market, especially for homes over $10 million, has been experiencing a downturn, this sale highlights ongoing interest in distinctive coastal properties.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Two California brothers face 35 felony charges each after hundreds complain of unfinished homes
item.description: A retired nurse in California paid more than $40,000 in 2023 for a backyard home that was never built. The company, Anchored Tiny Homes, later faced more than 200 complaints across 18 counties over unfinished projects and missing payments. Its founders, brothers Austin and Colton Paulhus, now face 35 felony charges each, while affected homeowners remain uncertain about recovering their money.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2012 and 2013, Maine removed two old Penobscot River dams to restore migratory routes; by September 2026, the Milford fish lift had counted a preliminary 5.85 million river herring returning upstream
item.description: In a significant ecological feat, the Penobscot River restoration in Maine has revitalized migratory fish numbers dramatically. The removal of the Great Works and Veazie dams has paved the way for essential fish migration pathways once again. As a result, the population of river herring has surged from just 556 to over 5 million.

item.title: Harris V Natural England: court faults regulator over Catfield Fen; campaigners eye next steps
item.description: In an impressive legal battle, two Norfolk farmers have secured a significant ruling for the Catfield Fen wetland, which faces threats from pollution. The High Court determined that Natural England neglected its duty to shield this vital habitat from agricultural runoff. The couple, who have invested approximately £1.5 million over the past 15 years to combat environmental challenges, stress the importance of strict enforcement of ecological regulations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A community in South Australia’s first dark-sky reserve is opposing a proposed hyperscale data centre; residents fear the development could change the rural landscape and threaten the darkness that draws visitors
item.description: Residents of Tungkillo, South Australia, are concerned about a proposed data centre that could disrupt their dark-sky reserve. The development may introduce light and noise pollution that affects the rural landscape. Community members believe preserving their unique nighttime environment is crucial for stargazing and natural experiences. The project's economic benefits are being weighed against potential environmental impacts. Ongoing discussions will determine the future of digital infrastructure in the region.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Dubai is growing coral in hotel lagoons before moving it back to the sea
item.description: In an ambitious effort to rejuvenate its marine life, Dubai is spearheading the Dubai Reef initiative, directed by the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism. The project focuses on restoring coral biodiversity along the coastal waters of the city. The Al Naseem nursery has successfully generated a variety of coral fragments that are being reintroduced into their natural habitat.
